I implemented `satisfies` and `maxSatisfying` in `src/semver.ts` by porting node-semver v7's version and range parsing, with default options. `bun test` passes (3 tests).

To check it further, I compared it with the real `semver@7.8.5` found in the local bun cache. A throwaway test at `/tmp/diff.test.ts` ran 60 ranges against 34 versions, covering all the range types in TASK.md plus invalid inputs, and also compared `maxSatisfying` for each range. All 2,135 checks matched. That comparison caught one 7.8 rule I had missed: ranges like `x.1.2` and `1.x.2` are invalid. I added that rule.

I didn't check against other 7.x releases, which may differ on edge cases like `x.1.2`. The comparison test isn't saved in the repo, because I wasn't allowed to edit `test/`.
